title: Question Tags: The Mirror Rule

vocab.ex: To be honest, it is not easy, is it?
Question tags follow the mirror rule.
A positive statement takes a negative tag.
A negative statement takes a positive tag.
This week has been exhausting, hasn't it?
You get along with your boss, don't you?
You are into football, aren't you?
We use tags to confirm information.
It's cold today, isn't it?
You're tired, aren't you?
You like pizza, don't you?
She works here, doesn't she?
He went home, didn't he?
You can swim, can't you?
She has finished, hasn't she?
They haven't left, have they?
I want you to agree with me.
We use tags to check information.
He gave up smoking last year.
That makes sense, doesn't it?
In present simple, use do/does for the tag.
At least it is Friday, right?
It is pretty cold today, isn't it?
I'm not sure, so I use a question tag.
Question tags are common in small talk.
It's a nice day, right?
You finished the report, correct?
Question tags sound friendly and natural.
Question tags make your English sound more natural.
I asked again just to double-check.

expressions.example: It's a beautiful day, isn't it?

sentences: It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
She works at the hospital, doesn't she?
He went to the party, didn't he?
You can speak Spanish, can't you?
They have finished the project, haven't they?

grammar.title: Question Tags: A Regra do Espelho
rules: Afirmação POSITIVA pede tag NEGATIVA: You're happy, aren't you?
Afirmação NEGATIVA pede tag POSITIVA: You aren't happy, are you?
A tag usa o MESMO verbo auxiliar da frase: You can swim, can't you? / She has left, hasn't she?
Sem auxiliar (presente/passado simples), use DO/DOES/DID: You like it, don't you? / He went, didn't he?

speak: It's a beautiful day, isn't it?
She works at the hospital, doesn't she?
You can speak Spanish, can't you?
They have finished the project, haven't they?
